data.description:
• Qualcomm has completed multiple fixed income offerings totaling several billion dollars and expanded its underwriter group, while also presenting its chip and connectivity roadmap at industry conferences in Miami and Munich during November 2026.
  • The business is absorbing weaker handset demand and the loss of Apple modem orders, and it is redirecting cash and talent toward AI and data center programs, including custom silicon for large cloud providers.

QUALCOMM Investment Narrative Recap

To own QUALCOMM today, you need to believe its AI, data center, automotive and IoT ambitions can gradually rebalance the business away from a softer handset market and the loss of Apple modem revenue. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St leans heavily on that mix shift. In the near term, the key catalyst is execution on early AI data center programs while the company absorbs weaker phone demand and higher memory costs.

The main risk right now is that AI and custom silicon spending runs ahead of confirmed orders, especially if smartphone volumes stay under pressure and free cash flow remains constrained. November’s bond deals and packed conference schedule appear to be more about preparing for that long investment cycle than signaling a material change to the immediate operating outlook.

The fixed income offerings in early November, including the US$1b 5.350% notes due 2031 and several US$750m tranches, matter most for funding those AI and data center build outs. QUALCOMM now has multi year capital locked in at known coupons, which can support heavier R&D and capacity commitments tied to its US$5b fiscal 2027 and US$15b fiscal 2029 AI data center revenue targets.

For you as a shareholder, that new debt stack raises the execution bar on projects such as the AWS custom silicon and optical connectivity agreement, which the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St views as a core driver of future non handset QCT revenue. If those design wins ramp more slowly than planned, higher interest costs and elevated operating expenses could weigh more heavily on earnings and keep valuation sensitive to any setback in AI centric programs.

QUALCOMM's narrative projects US$62.7b revenue and US$12.3b earnings by 2029, which implies forecast revenue growth of 13.3% per year and an earnings decline of US$1.3b from current earnings of US$13.6b.

Exploring Other Perspectives

One bearish angle on Qualcomm focuses on the risk that new AI data center custom chips come through on thinner margins, not just whether the US$5b and US$15b revenue goals are reached. The most cautious analysts were projecting about US$58.1b of sales and US$11.8b of earnings by 2029, yet still saw a sharply lower fair value. Those forecasts, along with the fresh bond deals and conference updates in Miami and Munich, did not exist in the same picture when those views were set, so you may want to compare both narratives and decide which assumptions feel closer to how you think Qualcomm’s story could evolve from here.

Harmony Gold Mining (JSE:HAR)

Overview: Harmony Gold Mining is a long established South African headquartered miner that produces gold and other metals across South Africa and Asia Pacific, offering direct exposure to physical gold production.

Operations: Harmony Gold Mining generates around ZAR 99.2b from gold, with about ZAR 79.5b from South Africa and ZAR 15.9b from international operations.

Market Cap: ZAR 146.5b

Harmony Gold Mining sits in this risk off gold screener because it is a large, liquid producer whose mine portfolio links directly to physical bullion. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St now frames the story around how that core gold exposure interacts with an emerging copper leg.

"The build out of Eva Copper and the volume ramp at CSA, with copper output targeted at about 100,000 tonnes per year by around 2029, could add a meaningful new revenue stream alongside gold and change Harmony Gold Mining’s earnings mix toward a higher copper contribution."

What happens if one unresolved cost and execution pressure pulls margins away from the tidy earnings path implied by consensus forecasts?

Those margin questions are exactly what the full narrative for Harmony Gold Mining tackles head on, including how copper could reshape Harmony Gold Mining’s risk and reward profile.

Alamos Gold (TSX:AGI)

Overview: Alamos Gold is a North American gold producer operating mines in Canada and Mexico, giving investors direct, relatively simple exposure to gold price moves.

Operations: Alamos Gold generates about $1.1b from the Island Gold District, $599 million from Mulatos and $585 million from Young Davidson.

data.title: We're Hopeful That ATEX Resources (TSE:ATX) Will Use Its Cash Wisely
data.description:
There's no doubt that money can be made by owning shares of unprofitable businesses. For example, biotech and mining exploration companies often lose money for years before finding success with a new treatment or mineral discovery. But while history lauds those rare successes, those that fail are often forgotten; who remembers Pets.com?

So should ATEX Resources (TSE:ATX) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? For the purpose of this article, we'll define cash burn as the amount of cash the company is spending each year to fund its growth (also called its negative free cash flow). Let's start with an examination of the business' cash, relative to its cash burn.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

When Might ATEX Resources Run Out Of Money?

A company's cash runway is the amount of time it would take to burn through its cash reserves at its current cash burn rate. When ATEX Resources last reported its September 2026 balance sheet in November 2026, it had zero debt and cash worth CA$133m. Looking at the last year, the company burnt through CA$55m. So it had a cash runway of about 2.4 years from September 2026. That's decent, giving the company a couple years to develop its business. The image below shows how its cash balance has been changing over the last few years.

See our latest analysis for ATEX Resources

How Is ATEX Resources' Cash Burn Changing Over Time?

Because ATEX Resources isn't currently generating revenue, we consider it an early-stage business. So while we can't look to sales to understand growth, we can look at how the cash burn is changing to understand how expenditure is trending over time. While it hardly paints a picture of imminent growth, the fact that it has reduced its cash burn by 26% over the last year suggests some degree of prudence. While the past is always worth studying, it is the future that matters most of all. So you might want to take a peek at how much the company is expected to grow in the next few years.

Can ATEX Resources Raise More Cash Easily?

While ATEX Resources is showing a solid reduction in its cash burn, it's still worth considering how easily it could raise more cash, even just to fuel faster growth. Generally speaking, a listed business can raise new cash through issuing shares or taking on debt. Commonly, a business will sell new shares in itself to raise cash and drive growth. By comparing a company's annual cash burn to its total market capitalisation, we can estimate roughly how many shares it would have to issue in order to run the company for another year (at the same burn rate).

ATEX Resources' cash burn of CA$55m is about 11% of its CA$516m market capitalisation. Given that situation, it's fair to say the company wouldn't have much trouble raising more cash for growth, but shareholders would be somewhat diluted.

So, Should We Worry About ATEX Resources' Cash Burn?

As you can probably tell by now, we're not too worried about ATEX Resources' cash burn. In particular, we think its cash runway stands out as evidence that the company is well on top of its spending. Its cash burn reduction wasn't quite as good, but was still rather encouraging! Based on the factors mentioned in this article, we think its cash burn situation warrants some attention from shareholders, but we don't think they should be worried.
